title.narrative: Anticipatory Action: Preparing for La Niña in Ayun, Wangey, Aware, and Daror Woredas of the Somali Region of Ethiopia

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project entitled " Anticipatory Action: Preparing for La Niña in Ayun, Wangey, Aware, and Daror Woredas of the Somali Region of Ethiopia" has been initiated with the purpose of enhancing the shock-resisting capacity of the community. Its main objective is to put in place preventive strategies to tackle the adverse effects of drought and support a total of 9,360 households, which amounts to over 62,710 individuals, considering an average household size of 6.7. The VSF-Suisse Anticipatory Action Project will be implemented in four districts within the Somali Region, including Ayun, Wangey, Aware, and Daror, over a period of six months. The total budget for this project is USD 575,977.02. The project aims to address the urgent humanitarian crisis faced by approximately 9.4 million individuals at high risk, exacerbated by the recent La Niña-driven drought. Forecasts predict below-average rainfall for the upcoming October-December season, posing a threat to the livelihoods of pastoral and agro-pastoral communities. The aftermath of the previous drought has resulted in a significant decline in livestock and crop production, amplifying the need for immediate intervention. This critical situation not only elevates the risk of malnutrition and disease outbreaks among vulnerable populations but also imperils children's education as families may turn to child labor to cope with economic pressures.ltbrgtTo confront these challenges, VSF-Suisse has outlined a series of livestock-related and agricultural interventions designed to enhance community resilience. These initiatives encompass mapping livestock diseases based on risks, delivering refresher training for animal health personnel, and implementing a voucher-based livestock treatment program. The project also underscores the importance of vaccinating against prioritized diseases and providing supplementary livestock feed to assist families during the drought. Additionally, the project will distribute farming tools for irrigation-based agriculture and promote hydroponic fodder production as an alternative source of income for women in the community. These actions are intended to complement existing WFP-funded projects in these woredas (with the exception of Daror) that concentrate on rangeland and water scheme rehabilitation to bolster community resilience and mitigate the anticipated impact of the drought in the Somali Region.ltbrgtlt/pgt
